slots.X: the structural explanation of Power of a Point theorem via cyclic similar triangles
slots.Y: two secants from external point P intersecting circle at A, B and C, D
slots.Z: cyclic quadrilateral angle subtension forces angle PAC = angle PDB; sharing angle P establishes similarity PAC ~ PDB
slots.W: Similar triangles PAC ~ PDB sharing angle P with angle PAC = angle PDB
slots.wrong_idea: claiming triangle PAC is similar to triangle PBC or invoking chord length formulas without angle invariants
slots.replacement_rule: cyclic quadrilateral ABDC has opposite angles summing to 180 deg, so angle PAC = angle PDB; with shared angle P, PAC ~ PDB yields PA/PD = PC/PB
slots.visual_job: render circle with secants PAB and PCD, highlighting similar triangles PAC and PDB; avoid unmounted SVGs
slots.check_job: continuity verification: as secant PCD rotates to tangent PT, points C and D coincide at T, giving PA * PB = PT^2
